t: Section 1022(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004 (Public Law 108–136; 10 U.S.C. 371 note) is amended by striking “and 2007” and inserting “through 2008”.

fable.w: This section only extends the fiscal-year range of an existing authority by replacing a date phrase. The tempting reading is that the underlying Section 1022 program might involve coordination with outside parties, but nothing in this text creates or requires consultation, a hearing, a comment period, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision here.
fable.s: is amended by striking “and 2007” and inserting “through 2008”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute, changing a date range. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely legislative housekeeping.
qwen_block.s: Section 1022(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004 (Public Law 108–136; 10 U.S.C. 371 note) is amended by striking “and 2007” and inserting “through 2008”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that extends the years an existing provision covers. It does not create a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue. Nobody outside the federal government takes part in any decision, so it is not participation.
opus.s: is amended by striking “and 2007” and inserting “through 2008”.
opus.b: The tempting reading would be to assume that, because this section amends a defense law, it might involve some process. It doesn't. The text only changes a date range. Section 1022(b) of the FY2004 National Defense Authorization Act deals with using counter-drug authorities and funds for counter-terrorism, and nothing in this amendment involves anyone outside the federal government.
